claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 can be solutionized into a single-phase homogeneous high-temperature BCC state.
Phase evolution during cooling and thermal exposure is governed primarily by a thermally activated, diffusion-controlled ordering reaction.
Al diffuses relatively rapidly in this alloy.
Al has a chemical-ordering tendency that induces local compositional fluctuations and short-range order.
Al-induced compositional fluctuations and short-range order nucleate ordered intermetallic phases from the BCC matrix.
The ordered phases produced may include B2 or D0₃ structures.
Differential element diffusivities, particularly enhanced Al mobility, cause local compositional partitioning during cooling.
Ordering lowers the local free energy by forming ordered structures within a metastable BCC matrix.
Cooling rate and subsequent thermal-exposure duration control the extent and length scale of ordering by regulating atomic mobility and available clustering time.
Intermediate-temperature holds at 600–800 °C provide sufficient atomic mobility for diffusional ordering.
Slow cooling or isothermal exposure at the target temperatures will produce detectable ordered phases relative to a rapidly quenched baseline.
The fraction of ordered domains will increase with longer isothermal dwell time and slower cooling.
The size of ordered domains will increase with longer isothermal dwell time and slower cooling.
Rapid quenching will largely preserve the homogeneous high-temperature BCC state with minimal ordering.
The proposed ordering mechanism operates only below the high-temperature homogenization limit where atomic mobility remains sufficient for ordering.
The proposed mechanism should not operate at temperatures far below the ordering onset or when diffusion is too limited.
Oxidizing conditions can introduce extrinsic effects that interfere with the proposed intrinsic ordering behavior.
A systematic absence of increased ordered-phase fraction or local ordering after slower cooling and longer thermal exposure would falsify the proposed mechanism.
